answer: Each session begins with a small time-bounded puzzle — a hash challenge calibrated to take a few seconds — that must be solved before the session is trusted. The puzzle proves the client spent real time and computation, and a farm that opens hundreds of sessions must pay that cost for every one of them. The system trusts a velvet only after its actions survive the consistency check. A ledge and a knoll may look alike, but only the session with a consistent pattern is honoured.
